::: {#sol-shift-test}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
cnn = train(make_cnn(), x_train, y_train)
mlp = train(make_mlp(), x_train, y_train)
cnn_acc = accuracy(cnn, x_test, y_test)
cnn_shift_acc = accuracy(cnn, shift_right(x_test), y_test)
mlp_acc = accuracy(mlp, x_test, y_test)
mlp_shift_acc = accuracy(mlp, shift_right(x_test), y_test)
print(cnn_acc, cnn_shift_acc, mlp_acc, mlp_shift_acc)
# The prose below says the MLP loses more; stop the render if it does not.
assert mlp_acc - mlp_shift_acc > cnn_acc - cnn_shift_acc
```

| Network | Test [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy) | Shifted test accuracy |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Convolutional | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$cnn_acc)` | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$cnn_shift_acc)` |
| [MLP](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-feedforward-network) | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$mlp_acc)` | `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * py$mlp_shift_acc)` |

The MLP loses more:
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (py$mlp_acc - py$mlp_shift_acc))` percentage points,
against `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (py$cnn_acc - py$cnn_shift_acc))` for the convolutional network.
The MLP has a separate weight for each pixel.
A stroke that moves to a new column meets weights trained on other strokes.
The [convolutional layers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-convolutional-layer) are [translation equivariant](#def-equivariance).
They find the same strokes one column over.
The [pooling](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-pooling) layer is not translation equivariant (@exm-equivariance).
The last linear layer has a separate weight for each pooled position,
as the MLP has for each pixel.

:::
